original_question: On which human chromosome is the gene located, mutations of which can cause the lethal form of Tetra-amelia syndrome because it prevents the formation of the lungs?

final_qi.question: On which human chromosome is the gene located, mutations of which can cause the lethal form of Tetra-amelia syndrome because it prevents the formation of the lungs?
final_qi.long_answer: The lethal form of Tetra-amelia syndrome with complete lung agenesis is caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the RSPO2 gene. RSPO2 lies at cytogenetic band 8q23.1 on human chromosome 8. Absence of functional RSPO2 disrupts WNT/β-catenin signalling that is essential for initiating both limb buds and lung buds, so embryos fail to develop limbs and lungs, leading to perinatal lethality. Hence, the responsible gene is located on chromosome 8.
